source:
Backyard Monsters is one of the most underappreciated strategy games ever made. It combined Clash of Clans, Factorio, tower defense, RTS, and idle progression years before most mobile games. The core loop was: build a monster base, gather resources, research new monsters, attack other players, and defend your own base while upgrades continued in real time.
I actually think a Roblox spiritual successor could be bigger than the original, because Roblox solves many of the social and multiplayer limitations that Facebook games had.

The Fantasy
You're not building a town.
You're growing a monster civilization hidden inside a suburban backyard.
Imagine:
 • gigantic mushrooms
 • monster nests
 • slime rivers
 • tree forts
 • toy blocks
 • abandoned bicycles
 • sprinklers become rivers
 • garden hoses become bridges
 • sandbox becomes a desert biome
The world feels gigantic because you're tiny.

Core Gameplay Loop

Login

↓

Collect resources

↓

Upgrade buildings

↓

Breed new monsters

↓

Scout nearby players

↓

Attack enemy bases

↓

Steal resources

↓

Expand territory

↓

Unlock stronger monsters

↓

Repeat

Every mechanic feeds this loop.

Layer 1 - Base Building
The base is your kingdom.
You start with

Monster Heart

Everything branches from it.
You place
Resource Extractors
Storages
Monster Housing
Walls
Turrets
Laboratories
Breeding Caves
Spell Towers
Decoration
Eventually
Huge Fortress

Resources
Instead of generic gold/elixir.
Make every resource thematic.
Example
Mush
Organic material.
Used for
 • buildings
 • walls

Goo
Monster food.
Used to
 • train monsters
 • breeding

Bones
Military resource.
Used for
 • advanced monsters
 • weapons

Electricity
Harvested from backyard electronics.
Used for
High-tech monsters.

Scrap
Found from
Broken toys
Soda cans
Old tools
Used for
Mechanical monsters.

Building Loop
Every building upgrades.
Level 1
Small nest.
Level 20
Massive fortress.
Visual progression matters.
Players LOVE seeing bases evolve.

Monster Collection
Instead of troops...
Think Pokémon meets Clash.
Each monster has

Role

Size

Element

Abilities

Movement

Housing Cost

Rarity

Examples
Tiny Gobbler
Fast melee.
Rock Rhino
Tank.
Spitter
Long-range acid.
Firefly
Flying DPS.
Mole
Burrows under walls.
Spider Queen
Summons babies.
Boom Beetle
Explodes.
Living Tree
Siege tank.
Dragon
Legendary.

Monster Classes

Common

Rare

Epic

Legendary

Ancient

Mythic

Not paywalled.
Obtained through
Research
Bosses
Events
Breeding
Exploration

Monster Progression
Each monster has
Level
Mastery
Mutations
Traits
Example
Fire Beetle
Level 1
↓
Level 20
↓
Mutation
Now explodes.
Later
Mutation
Leaves lava.

Research Tree
One of the best parts of Backyard Monsters.
Huge tech tree.
Example

Military

├── Faster monsters

├── Better AI

├── Larger armies

└── Flying units

Defense

├── Walls

├── Cannons

├── Traps

└── Shields

Economy

├── Storage

├── Mining

├── Production

└── Automation

Magic

├── Spells

├── Summons

├── Weather

└── Rituals

Research takes
Minutes
Hours
Days

Army Building
Instead of
"train 50 troops"
Players create squads.
Example
Squad Alpha
Tank
Tank
Healer
Healer
DPS
DPS
Flying
Flying
Each squad has a strategy.

Battle Gameplay
Here's where I'd improve massively.
Old Backyard Monsters was mostly click-and-watch.
Instead...
Hybrid RTS.
Player
Drops monsters.
Can
Ping targets.
Cast spells.
Retreat.
Use abilities.
Activate ultimate.
Enough control to feel involved.
Not enough to overwhelm.

Base Defense
Every base should feel unique.
Defenses include
Spike traps
Acid pools
Tesla towers
Slime launchers
Monster dens
Poison flowers
Giant Venus flytraps
Rocket squirrels
Laser garden gnomes
Everything fits the backyard theme.

Terrain Matters
Huge improvement.
Height matters.
Trees block vision.
Water slows.
Mud traps.
Sprinklers flood.
Tall grass hides units.
Sandbox slows heavy monsters.
Terrain creates strategy.

AI Behavior
Instead of dumb pathfinding.
Each monster has priorities.
Tank

Attack nearest defense

Protect allies

Taunt

Assassin

Ignore walls

Jump inside

Kill defenses

Escape

Healer

Stay behind

Heal lowest HP

Retreat

Makes every monster feel alive.

Exploration
The original mostly stayed around PvP.
I'd add PvE.
Outside your base
Procedurally generated backyard.
Find
Abandoned toys
Insect nests
Bird houses
Storm drains
Garages
Treehouses
Each biome contains
Resources
Bosses
Secrets
Rare monsters

World Map
Think
Backyard
↓
Neighborhood
↓
City Park
↓
Sewer
↓
School Playground
↓
Construction Site
↓
Shopping Center
↓
National Forest
World continually expands.

Bosses
Huge creatures.
Garden Snake
Lawn Mower
Cat
Dog
Crow
Spider Queen
Raccoon
Each drops
Unique monster DNA.

Breeding System
One of the biggest missing opportunities.
Example
Fire Beetle
 • 
Rock Rhino
↓
Lava Rhino
Players experiment.
Hundreds of combinations.
Like DragonVale meets Pokémon.

Seasons
Weather affects gameplay.
Rain
More Goo.
Winter
Frozen rivers.
Summer
Fire monsters stronger.
Autumn
Leaf camouflage.

Alliances
Neighborhood Monster Clubs.
Members
Donate monsters.
Share resources.
Raid bosses.
Alliance wars.
Alliance tech tree.
Alliance fortress.

PvP
Three modes.
Raid
Steal resources.
Ranked
Lose/gain trophies.
War
Alliance vs Alliance.

Reputation
Instead of trophies only.
Neighborhood Reputation.
Higher reputation unlocks
NPC traders.
Legendary bosses.
Special cosmetics.
Elite players.

Endgame
Not just bigger numbers.
Players chase
Monster encyclopedia completion
Perfect mutations
Rare decorations
Alliance rankings
Seasonal leaderboards
World bosses
Legendary base skins

Live Events
Weekly
Meteor crashes.
Alien invasion.
Backyard flooded.
Neighborhood barbecue.
Halloween monsters.
Christmas toy factory.
Every event changes gameplay.

Idle Progression
Offline
Resources continue.
Research continues.
Breeding continues.
Monster healing continues.
Expeditions continue.
Enough idle to respect players' time, but not so much that active play feels unnecessary.

Roblox-Specific Improvements
This is where a clone can become something much larger.
Instead of every player living in an isolated instance, imagine an entire persistent neighborhood server with 20-40 players.
Each player owns one backyard, but everyone can:
 • Walk to neighboring yards.
 • Watch live attacks.
 • Trade monster DNA.
 • Visit alliance fortresses.
 • Participate in neighborhood events (like defending against a giant cat invading multiple bases).
This makes the world feel alive in a way the original never could.

Technical Architecture

Server
├── Persistent World
├── Base Simulation
├── Resource Production
├── Combat Engine
├── Pathfinding
├── AI Behavior Trees
├── Research System
├── Alliance System
├── Matchmaking
├── Economy
└── Live Events

Client
├── Building Mode
├── RTS Controls
├── Combat VFX
├── Monster Animation
├── UI
├── Camera
└── Audio

Each player's base is an independently simulated "island" within the larger neighborhood, allowing efficient server performance while still supporting social interactions and live events.

Long-Term Retention
The best strategy games always have goals on multiple timescales:
 • 5-minute session: Collect resources, queue upgrades, check breeding results, attack one nearby base.
 • 30-minute session: Explore a new biome, defeat a boss, redesign your defenses, experiment with a new army composition.
 • Weekly goal: Complete alliance events, unlock a new monster family, climb ranked PvP, finish research branches.
 • Monthly goal: Earn limited seasonal monsters, evolve Ancient monsters, upgrade your fortress, and compete for neighborhood dominance.
The original Backyard Monsters proved that combining base building, asynchronous PvP, and long-term progression was compelling. A modern Roblox version could push that much further by emphasizing collectible monsters with unique AI, exploration beyond the home base, cooperative neighborhood gameplay, and a living world that changes through seasonal events rather than simply recreating the original formula.

answers.ask: Should we build one backyard base first, or the whole neighbourhood world map? Eight expanding world tiers will not fit in a single top-down image, so they would be separate maps.
answers.answer: Build one backyard base first as the playable vertical slice. The wider world map and its expanding tiers can come later as separate maps.

answers.ask: Are the neighbouring players' yards inside the same map as yours, or separate instances you travel to?
answers.answer: Neighbouring players' yards should be separate instances you travel to for scouting and raids, keeping each base focused and readable.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: Should we build one backyard base first, or the whole neighbourhood world map? Eight expanding world tiers will not fit in a single top-down image, so they would be separate maps. A: Build one backyard base first as the playable vertical slice. The wider world map and its expanding tiers can come later as separate maps.
- [author] shape — Q: Are the neighbouring players' yards inside the same map as yours, or separate instances you travel to? A: Neighbouring players' yards should be separate instances you travel to for scouting and raids, keeping each base focused and readable.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one large suburban backyard seen at tiny-monster scale as the first playable base-building vertical slice. Center the player's territory on a Monster Heart with broad open buildable ground radiating around it for resource extractors, storages, monster housing, walls, turrets, laboratories, breeding caves, spell towers, decorations, and eventual fortress growth. Make the backyard feel gigantic with towering mushrooms, monster nests, toy blocks, an abandoned bicycle, sprinklers feeding stream-like water, a garden hose used as a bridge, a sandbox reading as a desert patch, a tree-fort landmark, slime channels, mud, tall grass, and varied height. Preserve open dynamic routes for squads attacking from any direction, defensive chokepoints near the base perimeter, and clear terrain effects: trees block vision, water and sand slow movement, mud traps, and grass conceals. Build only this backyard now; do not attempt the later neighborhood, park, sewer, playground, construction, shopping, or forest maps.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy, specifically real-time base building and defense. Simulation is secondary because production, upgrades, breeding, and idle progression shape the base footprint.

## Shape and preset
Use `terrain-open`, named Open Contested Terrain: units path dynamically across one backyard rather than following a hard-coded lane. The preset is Real-Time Strategy, matching territorial building around a core and distributed thematic resource sites.

## Config requirements
Use `buildzone-plot` for broad proximity-gated construction ground around the Monster Heart. Use the visible side of `tracker-core` for the Heart itself. Use `cover-los` for trees and tall grass that block or conceal views, `choke-bottleneck` for hose crossings and defensive perimeter gaps, and `destructible-cluster` for breakable walls and fortifications. Use universal `terrain-relief` for tactically meaningful height and `water-body` for sprinkler streams and slime channels.

## Layout requirements
Place `tracker-core` at the defensible center of the yard. Use `collectible-nodes` for Mush, Goo, Bones, Electricity, and Scrap sites aligned to mushrooms, slime, remains, backyard electronics, and broken toys. Place `spawner-npc` raid origins around the outer yard boundary so attacks can approach from multiple directions. Reserve buildable footprints for economy, housing, research, breeding, defense, and eventual fortress upgrades without pre-filling every structure.

## Layout components
The current build is one backyard map only: central Heart territory, expandable build ground, defensive perimeter, distributed resource pockets, giant household props, tree fort, sandbox, hose bridge, water and slime channels, mud, grass, and relief. Neighboring yards and all wider world tiers are deferred separate instances, not additional segments in this vertical slice.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: make buildable territory, resource access, dynamic attack approaches, chokepoints, and terrain effects authoritative before dressing the tiny-scale backyard.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is large because a whole backyard must coexist with individually legible monster buildings and household props. The theme is a hidden monster civilization in a gigantic suburban backyard. Use `tiered` for tactical relief and `CHECK` for traversable sprinkler and slime water; the current vertical slice otherwise stays on one map.
